findings.F1: The coin's 24-hour return, measured against its 30-day average absolute 24-hour return, is followed by a rebound after the largest falls. When the 24-hour fall is 3 or more times the usual size, the coin rises more than its normal drift over the next 24 hours by +1.88 % per case (strength 0.38, t 4.49, 363 cases). Over the next 48 hours the figure is +2.47 % (strength 0.39, t 3.75, 172 cases). Both are about 10 to 13 times this backtest's 0.19 % round trip.
findings.F2: The rebound is graded by the size of the fall. Over the next 24 hours the excess is +0.07 % for falls of 0.7 to 1.3 times usual (t 0.64), +0.45 % to +0.41 % for falls of 1.3 to 3 times (t 3.0 and 1.7), and +1.88 % beyond 3 times. The rank correlation across all falls of 1.3 times or more is weak (rho 0.040, p 0.06, 2147 cases), so most of the effect sits in the extreme falls.
findings.F3: The 24-hour rebound after falls of 1.3 times usual or more appears on every coin. It is +0.15 % on BTC (t 0.67) and rises through ETH and LTC (t 1.7 each) to XMR, XRP and ZEC (+0.80 % to +1.09 %, t 2.5 to 2.9).
findings.F4: The rebound depends on the period. By year it is strong in 2018 (+1.44 %, t 3.43) and 2021 (+2.37 %, t 4.47), near zero in 2022 (-0.02 %, t -0.04), and positive but weaker in the other years. By window group it ranges from +0.18 % in w1 to w6 (t 0.91) to +1.49 % in w13 to w18 (t 4.07).
findings.F5: The rebound holds in both 7-day regimes. When the 7-day return is negative it is +0.74 % (t 4.66, 1604 cases); when it is positive, +0.51 % (t 2.53, 543 cases).
findings.F6: The tested idea's up surges do not continue in the short run. Over the next 24 hours, 24-hour rises of 2 to 3 times usual are followed by -0.37 % (t -1.96), and rises beyond 3 times by -0.34 % (t -1.07). Only over 120 hours, in a rising week, do surges above 2 times show +2.18 % (t 1.93, 167 cases), which cannot be told apart from chance given the number of angles examined.
findings.F7: The book's worst days come after the coin rose and are followed by the coin rebounding. On the book's worst-decile days the coin fell 6.13 % after a +1.34 % day before, then rose 0.69 % the next day (and the book 0.52 %). The book is long into falls and misses the rebound that F1 describes.
findings.F8: Two calendar patterns stand out, but neither yields a graded idea.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, is a fall several times its 30-day average absolute 24-hour return, the coin rises over the next 1 day by more than its usual 1-day return. The larger the fall against that average, the larger the rebound, with most of it after falls of about three times the usual size and more.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys a coin at the hour of an exceptional 24-hour fall and holds for a day, sized up with the size of the fall, and refuses to sell into it.
ideas.name: rebound after extreme daily falls

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, is a fall several times its 30-day average absolute 24-hour return, the coin rises over the next 2 days by more than its usual 2-day return. The larger the fall against that average, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader who buys an exceptional 24-hour fall holds it for two days, because the rebound keeps building past the first day.
ideas.name: two-day rebound after crashes
